story.title: Trump Dismisses Iran's Proposal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
story.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear negotiations. Trump stated that the deal was not acceptable, expressing a desire for a better agreement. Iranian officials, while aware of Trump's comments, noted they had not received a formal rejection of the plan. Iran's Foreign Minister indicated that the country is prepared for renewed conflict but remains open to diplomatic solutions.

event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people physically harmed by the September 11, 2001 attacks or related debris-removal work, and for representatives of people who died as a result. It is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice through a Special Master and remains a central avenue for eligible survivors, responders, residents, workers, and families affected by 9/11-related illness or death.

facts.label: Origin and purpose
facts.value: Congress created the original VCF on September 22, 2001, under Title IV of the Air Transportation Safety and System Stabilization Act to compensate individuals physically injured in the attacks and personal representatives of those killed.

facts.label: Current legal framework
facts.value: The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reopened and expanded the fund in 2011; the 2019 Never Forget the Heroes Act permanently authorized it, set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline, and appropriated the funding needed for approved claims.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The VCF is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice and its Special Master; as of the VCF's 2026 public materials, the Special Master is Allison Turkel.

facts.label: Eligible exposure locations
facts.value: Claims may cover qualifying exposure at the World Trade Center and designated New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 to May 30, 2002; the Pentagon through November 19, 2001; or Shanksville, Pennsylvania through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Eligibility and claim type
facts.value: Generally, an applicant must establish presence at a covered site during the relevant period and a certified 9/11-related physical condition; authorized personal representatives may bring claims for deceased victims, including personal-injury and, where applicable, wrongful-death compensation.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows news and commemorations connected to the 25th anniversary of the attacks, including advocacy and records-related developments, rather than providing a complete account of VCF claims, awards, health-program coverage, or all 9/11-related events.

explore_lenses.label: What terms are blocking a Hormuz reopening?
explore_lenses.title: The dispute is over a broader package, not just shipping
explore_lenses.summary: Iran’s reported seven-day proposal ties reopening the strait to a ceasefire and economic relief, while Trump said the offer itself was unacceptable. The public accounts do not establish a mutually agreed text or a formal U.S. counteroffer.

claims.text: CBS reported that Iran’s proposal called for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting nuclear negotiations within seven days, while seeking an end to fighting across the Middle East, including Lebanon, and relief affecting Iranian oil sales and ports.

Trump said on September 26 that he was rejecting Iran’s deal, though he also said he favored making a deal; CBS reported that Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff had participated in talks with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

Treasury’s Operation Economic Outcast says the U.S. is expanding sanctions and secondary-sanctions risk to isolate Iran economically, indicating that sanctions relief is a central point of leverage rather than a settled concession.

explore_lenses.label: What changed for ships and oil flows?
explore_lenses.title: Shipping remains disrupted despite limited escorted movement
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate operational picture is not a return to normal navigation: U.S. officials describe escorted departures, while official U.S. economic material says Hormuz shipping has remained below pre-conflict levels. Regional governments are pressing for unimpeded passage.

claims.text: Trump said 29 vessels had exited the strait under U.S. military supervision; this is a presidential claim reported by CBS, not an independently documented measure of normal commercial traffic.
A Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee report said shipping through Hormuz had stayed below pre-conflict levels and that oil prices remained sensitive to developments in the conflict.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan called at the U.N. for protection of freedom of navigation and restoration of conditions in Hormuz to those before February 28, without fees or taxes, according to CBS reporting.
Oman’s foreign minister called for restraint and dialogue and said Muscat was ready to mediate and continue efforts to safeguard navigation in the strait, according to CBS.

story_report.summary: President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, resume nuclear negotiations and lift the U.S. naval blockade, saying he wanted a better agreement. Iran said it had seen Trump’s public comments but had not received a formal response through mediators. The result is an immediate diplomatic impasse over the strait, while Tehran says it remains open to negotiations but is prepared for renewed conflict.

sections.heading: Iran Proposal Links Talks and Relief
sections.body: CBS reported that Iran’s proposal sought the reopening of Hormuz and a restart of nuclear negotiations within seven days, alongside an end to fighting across the Middle East, including Lebanon. It also sought relief affecting Iranian oil sales and ports. The terms place economic pressure at the center of the dispute: Treasury says its Operation Economic Outcast will continue targeting Iranian revenue, sanctions-evasion and procurement networks.

sections.heading: Hormuz Traffic Remains Below Normal
sections.body: Trump said 29 vessels had exited the strait under U.S. military supervision, but CBS characterized that as a presidential claim rather than an independently documented measure of normal commercial traffic. A Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee report said shipping through Hormuz remained below pre-conflict levels and oil prices were sensitive to developments in the conflict. Saudi Arabia has called for restored freedom of navigation without fees or taxes, while Oman has urged restraint and dialogue.

sections.heading: Mediation Offer Lacks Public Framework
sections.body: Oman has publicly offered to mediate and continue efforts to safeguard navigation, but there is no confirmation that Washington and Tehran have accepted an Omani process. Araghchi said Tehran would decide after receiving definitive positions through mediators. Senator John Kennedy said the United States would need either a settlement reopening the strait or escalation, while adding that he would not support sending troops; that was his assessment, not an administration decision.

unresolved.text: The detailed proposal, U.S. requirements for any revised agreement and whether a formal American response has been delivered through intermediaries have not been made public.
No public, independently verified accounting establishes current Hormuz transits, the scope of Iranian restrictions or the conditions needed for commercial traffic to resume at scale.
No formal timetable has been announced for mediator-led talks, sanctions changes, a ceasefire or an operation to reopen the strait.

related_stories.title: Pope Leo XIV Visits Lourdes, Addresses Clergy Abuse and Healing
related_stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV is on a four-day visit to France, having recently prayed at the Grotto of Massabielle in Lourdes, a significant pilgrimage site. He is set to meet privately with survivors of clerical sexual abuse, following a French inquiry that revealed extensive abuse within the Church. During his visit, the Pope emphasized the need for the Church to confront its past and heal 'deep wounds' while also criticizing assisted dying as 'false compassion.'
